kind: code (Phase 9 SERIAL — adapter/tools.ts). THREE tools: conductor_mark_green (TEST_VETTED->GREEN, and PENDING->GREEN for a non-behavioral item), conductor_validate (GREEN->VALIDATED, the full required-scope verify with the §4.2 foreign-red quarantine, plus the DEBUG protocol on failure), and conductor_queue_amend (re-validates the amended queue and records a §2.7 decision). New handler exports follow the established handleX convention.

specGaps: GAP (does mark_green DISPATCH the implementer, or is it called after one?): §3.3 says the implementer 'may now edit the item's fileScope' and 'the handler re-runs the item test itself; exit 0 required'. PROPOSED: mark_green owns the WHOLE stage exactly as 9.4a's submit_test owns PENDING->RED — dispatch the implementer (role 'implementer', writeCapable, schema ImplementerResult, doctrine tdd.md), then run the item test ITSELF and admit through the core edge. This is the one reading under which 'the implementer never runs done by assertion' is enforceable rather than advisory.

GAP (the §3.3 BLOCKED escalation ladder — 'more context -> stronger model -> item re-split via conductor_queue_amend -> surfaced to the human'): the middle rung is NOT CONSTRUCTIBLE from §2.1, which has models.roles (a role->model map) but no notion of a stronger escalation model, and the re-split rung would have mark_green call queue_amend, which the 9.4b bullet does not ask for. PROPOSED: implement the two constructible rungs — NEEDS_CONTEXT re-dispatches ONCE carrying what was asked for (the C-032 D9 shape), and BLOCKED (or a spent budget) raises ONE §2.11 question on the existing 'implementer-blocked' origin and blocks the item, whose answer is where a human directs a re-split. The two unimplementable rungs are RAISED AT THE PHASE 9 GATE rather than faked, since a 'stronger model' rung with no knob to name the model would be a stub (G4).

GAP (runTest's no-template fallback is named as a quarantine site but has no way to be one): §4.2 line 1582 lists 'runVerify (and runTest's no-template fallback, and publish's auto re-verify, and conductor_report's closing verify)' as the four sites that quarantine the foreign red set — but the committed RunTestOptions carries no exclusion parameter, so the fallback currently runs the whole suite including other items' deliberate reds. This is what the 'two no-template items in one wave without livelocking' row exercises. PROPOSED: extend adapter/evidence.ts runTest with the same excludeTestFiles the verify path takes, quarantining through the SAME quarantine.ts helpers. NOTE the interaction with C-032 D1: the handler now refuses an untargeted red whose excerpt names no testScope file, and the quarantine is exactly what makes a no-template fallback name the item's OWN file — the two are complementary, and without the quarantine a no-template item could never legally go red at all.

GAP (what hypothesis does the first DEBUG entry record?): §2.5 setDebugging takes {hypothesis} and §3.3 requires root-cause-before-fix. PROPOSED: the first failure records a hypothesis derived from the verify's OWN captured failure (the failing scope + excerpt), never a model paraphrase; subsequent rounds carry the implementer's stated hypothesis. Asserted on the persisted item, not on prompt text.

GAP (conductor_queue_amend's decision shape): §2.7 records need >=2 scored options for kind 'derived'. PROPOSED: kind 'derived' with the amendment and the leave-as-is arm both scored, gated by the SAME core requireTwoOptions every other decision site runs (the C-032 F7 lesson: enforce at the write, do not assert in a comment).

assertions.text: conductor_mark_green re-runs the ITEM TEST ITSELF and DENIES on a non-zero exit: the item stays at TEST_VETTED, no GREEN transition is persisted, and the implementer's DONE receipt does not advance it — 'done by assertion' is refused, asserted against a real child process and a real ledger append
a passing item test advances TEST_VETTED->GREEN through core legalItemTransition, persists the §2.6 green pointer on the item, and journals the transition through the closed §7.4 vocabulary

conductor_mark_green from PENDING is LEGAL for a behavioral:false item and runs NO item test at all — asserted by the ABSENCE of any new §2.6 record for the item plus an unexecuted-command sentinel, not by a missing log line (a behavioral:true item at PENDING is still refused, naming conductor_submit_test)

conductor_validate reaches GREEN->VALIDATED through adapter/evidence.ts runVerify — the quarantine, start-stamp, HEAD record and per-tree marker are all runVerify's, asserted by observing its effects (the §2.6 verify record carries the start stamp and HEAD; the marker file existed during the run and is gone after) rather than by 9.4b re-implementing any of them

a second conductor_validate against a tree holding a LIVE verify marker is DENIED naming the running verify, runs no scope, and leaves the holder's marker byte-identical (two verifies in one tree would each describe a tree the other was mutating)

while the verify is in flight the freeze gate denies EVERY edit in that tree — production files and test files alike — asserted THROUGH the real edit gate / §5.3 wiring against a live marker, and the same edit is allowed once the marker is gone

item A's validate goes GREEN despite THREE foreign red tests, in one test per case so a handler that unions only some of them fails: (a) a wave sibling at RED, (b) a BLOCKED prior-wave item at RED, (c) a §2.11 stale-red registry entry left by an EARLIER RUN (the case no in-run rule could have caught — the registry is the only witness). Each foreign file is proven to have been moved OUT of the repo and restored afterwards

the quarantine NEVER excludes the item's own tests: with item A's OWN test red, A's validate FAILS — the same fixture as the row above with only the failing file's ownership changed, so a handler that quarantined everything red would pass one and fail the other

TWO items in one wave whose verify scope has NO §2.1 itemTest template both reach GREEN: each one's fallback run quarantines the OTHER's red test, so neither is blocked by its sibling and the wave does not livelock (without the quarantine each item's run fails on the other's test forever). Asserted end-to-end against real child processes

a failing validate enters the DEBUG protocol: item.debugging is persisted with a hypothesis derived from the verify's OWN captured failure, the item does NOT advance, and doctrine debug.md is injected into the implementer's NEXT dispatch — asserted by finding debug.md's real content in the dispatched prompt (loaded through the committed pack loader, never a literal)

at config.workflow.debugFixCap failed fixes the item is BLOCKED and exactly ONE §2.11 question is written on the EXISTING origin 'debug-architecture' (the closed vocabulary is not widened), naming the failures that motivated the escalation; the cap is read from config and asserted at TWO different values so a hardcoded count fails

conductor_queue_amend re-runs core validateQueue over the AMENDED queue and REFUSES an amendment that introduces a dependsOn cycle, an intersecting fileScope, or a behavioral/testScope violation — nothing is persisted on a refusal (legality before persist), and the queue on disk is byte-identical

an accepted amendment persists the new queue AND appends one §2.7 kind:'derived' decision naming what changed, gated by the SAME core requireTwoOptions every other decision site runs (a <2-scored-options amendment is rejected and NOTHING is persisted)
